newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's CiU ready to back 1998 budget law.
newsitem.headline: Spain's CiU ready to back 1998 budget law.

text.p: Spanish government ally Catalan Convergencia i Unio said on Thursday it was ready to back the 1998 budget law, which is designed to ensure Spain's prompt entry into European economic and monetary union.
CiU economic spokesman Francesc Homs told Reuters in a interview he did not see any problem which could put the approval of the Spanish 1998 budget at risk.
"I think there won't be any problem that could put budget approval at risk," he said.
He said the new budget law forecasts a 3.5 percent increase in 1998 gross domestic product and a 2.0 percent rise in consumer inflation.
He said the CiU expected a solid increase in public investment as well.

"In the next half of 1997 the government will have significant revenues from its privatisation process and the same will be true in 1998," he said, adding that this money would be used in the reduction of debt and in public investment.
For public investment, 1997 has been a transition year.
"The 1998 budget will reveal increased privatisation receipts which will be used both to pay back debt and for public investment."
The ruling minority Popular Party government needs the CiU's legislative votes to pass the budget. The CiU backs the PP in an alliance but is not part of the government.
